title: kv-cache: fragmentation-aware eviction + paging/spillover scheduling optimizations
author: Priya Mehta
title_and_description:
kv-cache: fragmentation-aware eviction + paging/spillover scheduling optimizations

Motivation: high-memory workloads and long-tail sequence lengths were triggering suboptimal KV cache behavior in production leading to increased GPU memory pressure, frequent spill-to-host cycles, and occasional latency p99 regressions under bursty traffic. This PR introduces a set of complementary changes to reduce fragmentation, improve paging/spillover scheduling, and make eviction decisions aware of both physical fragmentation and effective reuse probability.

What Changed:
- Add fragmentation-aware memory accounting: track contiguous segment allocation metadata per allocation slab so we can estimate fragmentation overhead and prefer compaction candidates that free contiguous space.
- Adaptive spillover thresholds: dynamic host spill thresholds now consider active batch size distribution and ongoing KV cache IO bandwidth to avoid thrashing under bursty traffic.
- Compaction + eviction pipeline: introduce background compaction pass that coalesces small freed segments during low utilization windows, with a priority queue that prefers high-reuse keys to remain resident.
- Eviction heuristic rewrite: combine LRU-ish recency with reuse-score and fragmentation-cost to compute eviction priority score. Weightings are configurable and auto-tuned using runtime telemetry.
- Scheduling improvements: an opt-in scheduling policy that staggers large evictions and spill IO across GPU worker threads to avoid synchronized pauses.
- Continuous batching integration: KV cache now exposes fast-path hints to the batching layer so requests likely to hit compacted regions are batched preferentially, minimizing cache-miss induced latency.
- Telemetry and observability: new metrics (kvcache.fragmentation_ratio, kvcache.compaction_events, kvcache.spill_io_ms, kvcache.eviction_score_distribution) and dashboards.
- Tests and benchmarks: microbenchmarks for various sequence length distributions and a canary config for staging that simulates multi-tenant bursty workloads.

Why this approach:
- Prior work on naive LRU and simple size-based eviction left worst-case fragmentation unhandled; by making fragmentation an explicit cost in eviction scoring and adding background compaction we reduce the need for emergency spillovers.
- Scheduling/staggering prevents synchronized evictions that spike tail latency.

benchmark_results: Microbench: multi-tenant bursty workload (100k keys, seq_len distribution heavy-tail): baseline p99 latency 286ms, after changes p99 198ms (30.7% reduction); avg token throughput +12%
Memory: fragmentation_ratio reduced from 0.37 to 0.12 on heavy churn tests; effective resident set increased ~18% for same logical keyset
Spill IO: median spill_io_ms reduced from 23ms to 9ms due to decreased frequency and staged spill scheduling
review_comments: Ethan Zhou: Overall this looks good. Two concerns: (1) the compaction pass could become CPU heavy on small-hosted instances — can we add a rate limiter? (2) how do we prove safety for concurrent access during compaction?
Priya Mehta (author): Addressed both. Added compaction_rate_limit config and switched compactor to copy-on-write for live keys; unit tests added to validate no corruption under concurrent readers.
Lina García: Approving after small nits. Please add backfill docs describing how to interpret kvcache.fragmentation_ratio in Console.
Priya Mehta: Added docs/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction.md and updated dashboards. Also added an alert kvcache.fragmentation_ratio>0.3 for 5m as a safe guard.
Marco Silva: Observability LGTM. CI had a flaky test in scheduling — reran and passed. Approving.
release_notes: Improved KV cache eviction and compaction: reduces fragmentation, lowers p99 latency under bursty workloads, and decreases spill IO. Feature behind feature flag kv_cache_eviction_v18. See runbook for rollout guidance.
canary_plan: Enable kv_cache_eviction_v18 on 1-2 Dedicated pools for 48h, monitor kvcache.fragmentation_ratio, kvcache.spill_io_ms, and p99 latency on sample routes; rollback if fragmentation_ratio increases or spill_io_ms regresses >10%.
followups: ENG-2212: autotune weighting for reuse vs fragmentation across workload clusters
